newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen mostly steady with a weak tone, amid lighter packer demand, livestock dealers said.

Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota were seen ranging from $55.00 to $55.50 per cwt while Illinois top prices could range from $53.50 to $54.00. Indiana/Ohio values at the plant were seen at $53.50 to $54.00.
Mixed pork prices at midday Wednesday spurred talk that weak pork demand would spur reduced packer buying, including lighter slaughter during the weekend, market sources said.

USDA at midday quoted 17-20 lb hams mostly $2.00 per cwt lower, with trimmings steady to $1.00 lower. Pork bellies were quoted steady to $2.00 higher. There were 25.5 pork loads and 42.0 loads of pork trimmings reported sold.

Cash hog prices could fall Thursday if pork prices end mostly lower Wednesday, particularly with pork production below last week, sources noted. Lower prices on lower supplies suggest soft retail demand, they said.
USDA pegged Wednesday's hog slaughter at 357,000 head, with the week-to-date figure at 1.038 million head, 3.6 percent below a week ago and 2.2 percent lower than last year.
